WHAT IS COVERED WELL
The nine UI lanes cover every in-app surface (shell, queue, history, sign-in, workspace, viewer, pull page, service status, copy, accessibility, prior art) with about 200 findings and about 900 screenshots. The design-lab scaffold already has a verified primitive guide (apps/lab/docs/primitives.md, 2,600 lines, with pitfalls such as "There is no \"primary\" color") and a fixture layer (apps/lab/docs/fixtures.md). So I do not ask for a primitive API lane.

WHAT IS MISSING (five gaps, most valuable first)
1. Real data. All lanes used synthetic data: 4 to 24 items, 600 x 400 images, short names. The one production read (audit/live-authenticated.md) shows 626 items, 3,832 variants, names such as `ariakit-tailwind-7466/applied-light-week-hover`, no titles. The lab "large" scenario has 120 items and 600 variants and has fields that production never sends. Many findings are only "partly-confirmed" for this reason.
2. Contract and earlier decisions. Verifiers of six lanes wrote "the binding contract was not consulted". No lane read docs/simplification-audit/contract-issue-1.md:247-281 (layout order, state rules, keyboard table), the earlier UI decision records (index.html #U01 to #U06, evidence/feedback-ui.md), or docs/design-r9.html. No lane owns the keyboard map, and lane proposals collide (for example `[` for swipe and for the sidebar).
3. Failures over time. No lane tested a tab that stays open: a deploy (route chunks are lazy, `rg preloadError apps/web/src` finds nothing, production answers 404 text/html for a missing asset), an expired session, a superseded run, two tabs, offline, receipts after reload, the OAuth error page. Pieces exist in four lanes but no error-to-screen matrix.
4. Surfaces outside the app. No lane read the GitHub check output. There are two check names and at least ten titles (packages/security/src/checks.ts:4-55, apps/web/src/api/pre-run-*.ts, operations/review-links.ts). `needs-review` maps to conclusion `failure` with the title "Visual review has not passed" (packages/service/src/run-status.ts:98-104). No lane followed a contributor without write access, the sign-in round trip, or the wait from the last approval to a green check.
5. Other browser engines. All lanes are Chrome-only. I ran Firefox 155 and WebKit (Safari 26.6) from the installed Playwright browsers: both load the fixture with no page error, and differences show at once. Firefox draws the stage checkerboard as triangles and the progress bar blue on white; WebKit and Chrome draw it green.

FOUND IN PASSING (not in any lane)
- "Approve & next" is 34.5 px high in dark and 32.5 px in light, and the first image starts at y 432 in dark and 429 in light, in all three engines. The layout changes with the color scheme.

- Visual language and icons: partly covered (PRIM-07, PRIM-13, PRIM-16, SHELL-20, A11Y-21) and the lab has Look controls. No lane made an icon inventory (about 20 Lucide icons); the design phase can do it.
- CLI text (the packages lane has it), a real screen reader, a real touch device, and all performance topics (other track).

PROCESS GAPS FOR THE WRITE-UP
- Four lanes have no report.md: ui-dashboard, ui-workspace, ui-viewer, ui-benchmark. Three have a recovered copy under verify/. ui-benchmark has none on disk; its text exists only in the structured summary.

gaps.title: Long-open tabs and failure recovery: deploy skew, expired sessions, state that changes under the page, and the error-to-screen matrix
gaps.prompt:
ROLE
You are the auditor for the lane `gap-session-resilience` (finding prefix RESIL) of the UI and UX audit of Visonaut. Nine UI lanes looked at each page in the state that it has right after load. No lane tested what a maintainer sees when a tab stays open and something changes: a deploy, an expired session, a new push, another reviewer, a lost connection. Test these cases and build one matrix from server error to screen.

ROOT = /Users/diegohaz/Developer/visonaut/.claude/worktrees/serialized-dazzling-pixel . Repository paths below are relative to ROOT.

WHY THIS LANE EXISTS (facts that the completeness critic checked)
- Route code is loaded on demand. The existing build has `runs._runId-*.js`, `pulls._pullNumber-*.js`, `routes-*.js`, and `preload-helper-*.js` in apps/web/dist/client/assets. `rg "preloadError" apps/web/src` finds nothing. gaps.title: Firefox and Safari (WebKit): rendering, keyboard, and focus behavior that every lane tested only in Chrome
gaps.prompt:
ROLE
You are the auditor for the lane `gap-cross-browser` (finding prefix XBR) of the UI and UX audit of Visonaut. Nine UI lanes captured about 900 screenshots and ran all behavior probes in Chrome only. Test the same UI in Firefox and in WebKit (the Safari engine), and report each difference in rendering, keyboard behavior, and focus behavior.

ROOT = /Users/diegohaz/Developer/visonaut/.claude/worktrees/serialized-dazzling-pixel . Repository paths below are relative to ROOT.

WHY THIS LANE EXISTS (facts that the completeness critic checked)
- Each lane lists "Chrome only" under items not verified. ui-primitives: "Firefox, and Safari were not tested. The recipes contain specific code for all of them." ui-shell: "The header glider depends on CSS anchor positioning." ui-a11y: "Firefox 'search for text when you start typing' and Safari were not tested against the single-key shortcuts." The lab fixture guide says its mask images are "verified in Chrome only" (apps/lab/docs/fixtures.md:117).
- The browsers are installed. The repository has Playwright 1.63.0, which needs firefox revision 1543 and webkit revision 2359. Both are in /Users/diegohaz/Library/Caches/ms-playwright. The critic launched both: Firefox 155 and WebKit with a Safari 26.6 user agent load http://127.0.0.1:4311/src/review/__tests__/index.html with no page error, and `CSS.supports("anchor-name: --a")` is true in both.
- First differences, seen in a 5 minute probe (screenshots in /Users/diegohaz/.claude/jobs/f65a6229/tmp/audit/ui-critic/screens/):
  1. Firefox draws the stage background as triangles, not as a checkerboard (stage-corner-firefox-dark-2x.png against stage-corner-chromium-dark-2x.png). The source is the `repeating-conic-gradient` in apps/web/src/components/screenshot-viewer.tsx:134.
  2. The native `<progress>` in the run header (apps/web/src/review/review-workspace.tsx:599-604) is blue on a white track in Firefox (progress-firefox-dark-2x.png), green on gray in WebKit, and green in Chrome.
  3. Not an engine difference, but new: "Approve & next" is 34.5 px high in the dark scheme and 32.5 px in the light scheme, the variant strip is 38 px against 36 px, and the first image starts at y 432 against 429. This is the same in Chrome, Firefox, and WebKit.

HOW TO RUN
The screenshot helper shot.mjs supports Chrome only. Write your own script:

   const { chromium, firefox, webkit, devices } = createRequire("/Users/diegohaz/Developer/visonaut/.claude/worktrees/serialized-dazzling-pixel/package.json")("@playwright/test");
   const browser = await firefox.launch();            // or webkit.launch(), or chromium.launch({ channel: "chrome" })
   const page = await browser.newPage({ viewport: { width: 1440, height: 900 }, colorScheme: "dark" });

For the phone layout in WebKit use `devices["iPhone 15"]`. For Firefox preferences use `firefox.launch({ firefoxUserPrefs: { ... } })`.

TASKS
A. State matrix. Capture the same states in Chrome, Firefox, and WebKit, dark and light, at 1440 x 900, and at 390 x 844 for the phone states. Use the workspace fixture and the route fixture with page.route mocks (the capture scripts of earlier lanes show how: /Users/diegohaz/.claude/jobs/f65a6229/tmp/audit/ui-workspace/capture.mjs, ui-dashboard/capture.mjs, ui-pull-ops/capture.mjs). States: sign-in, forbidden, queue with 8 runs, history with 8 runs, service status with alerts, bell popover, account menu, pull page pending, workspace default, many variants, Details open, Difference mode, 200% zoom, whole-item dialog, keyboard help dialog, status filter popover open, search with text, read-only run, save error, loading state, phone default, phone item dialog. For each state compute a pixel difference against Chrome (pixelmatch is in the repository dependencies) to rank the states, then READ the images and describe each real difference. Ignore pure font anti-aliasing noise, and say so.
B. Rendering checks, each with a measurement in three engines: the stage checkerboard; the native progress element (computed appearance and colors); the native select and the search input in the history view (WebKit search decoration); `image-rendering: pixelated` at 100% and 200% (zoom a crop and read it); gliders that use anchor positioning (header nav, variant strip, view mode group: position and size against the selected element); popover and dialog enter animation and position; sticky bars and `dvh` units; the 64rem container query against the 1023 px media query (findings SHELL-11 and A11Y-03); scrollbar width (innerWidth minus clientWidth) and what a classic scrollbar does to the layout; text metrics (the theme names "Inter Variable" and the app ships no font, finding PRIM-16: record the rendered font and the width of the same heading in each engine); focus ring shape and clipping (findings A11Y-08, A11Y-09, PRIM-20).
C. Keyboard and focus checks in each engine:
   1. Each shortcut of the review workspace (A, X, Shift+A, Shift+X, S, D, F, G, arrows, 1 to 6, `[`, Cmd or Ctrl+Z). Record what the page does and what the browser does.
   2. Firefox with `accessibility.typeaheadfind` on ("Search for text when you start typing"), and the Firefox quick find keys `/` and `'`. Do the page shortcuts still work? Does the find bar open?
   3. Tab order in WebKit with Tab and with Alt+Tab. Safari does not move focus to links with Tab by default. The item rows, the variant chips, the header links, and "Queue" are links. Count the Tab stops and name the controls that Tab cannot reach. Compare with the 30 stops that the workspace lane measured in Chrome (finding WORK-29).
   4. Focus after a mouse click on a button, a link, and a variant chip. Safari and Firefox on macOS can leave focus on the body after a click on a button. Re-test the two high findings that depend on click focus: shortcuts stop after a click on a variant chip (WORK-01, A11Y-01), and focus after a decision and after Undo (A11Y-02).
   5. `:focus-visible` after a click and after a key press on the same control.
   6. Back and forward (page cache) on the queue and the run page: is the state restored, is a request sent?
   7. The readiness gate: `img.decode()` and the dimension check in apps/web/src/components/screenshot-viewer.tsx:49-72 with a slow image and with a broken image.
D. The scheme difference of item 3 above. Find the cause (for example a border that exists in one scheme only). List each element whose box size differs between dark and light on the queue and on the workspace.
